central_topic: Coverage and interval-width tradeoffs for binary superpopulation mean inference from fixed labeled and unlabeled samples and a frozen scalar predictor, using honest nonlinear score controls against prediction-powered and labeled-only intervals.
core_methods: Two-fold cross-fitted residual correction with frozen-score control variates and finite-unlabeled-sample weighting N/(n+N)
Train-fold-only clipped ridge affine and piecewise-linear spline calibration selected by generalized cross-validation
Wilson-style stabilized asymptotic Wald inference, with a sample-size-only Clopper-Pearson fallback for n<16
Separately implemented bounded empirical-Bernstein component intervals with union-bound aggregation; not evaluated as the primary output
Conditional-mean control-variate oracle and nonlinear-versus-affine variance frontier; theoretical context, not measured oracle attainment
result_driven_themes: Across seven anonymous cases repeated over 256 seeds, candidate-minus-PPI++ mean width is negative only in case 2 and positive in the other six; there is no universal narrowing result.

In case 5, truth is approximately 0.0068; the implemented PPI++ comparator has coverage 0.55078125 and 115 zero-width intervals out of 256, motivating boundary and rare-event inference literature rather than treating narrow invalid intervals as gains.
Final aggregate candidate coverage is 0.9425223214285714; casewise uncertainty and non-rejection of nominal coverage do not establish exact 95% validity.
Finite-sample safety bounds and the nonlinear-versus-affine frontier are source-supported context, not experimentally established safety-track efficiency or spline superiority.

queries.rationale: Explicitly permitted starter reference for cross-fitting and orthogonal-score principles. The candidate fits score calibrators on complementary labeled folds; this is methodological context, not a causal estimand or an experimentally evaluated DML baseline.

The implemented estimator uses labeled residual means plus unlabeled control means with N/(n+N) weighting. METHOD.md and study.py state a conditional-mean oracle variance and affine-projection gap, grounding a narrowly scoped efficiency-literature query without claiming oracle attainment.

ScoreCalibrator implements ridge affine and piecewise-linear spline candidates with train-fold quantile knots and generalized cross-validation. Retrieve foundational calibration machinery, not deep-model architecture comparisons or an unsupported empirical spline-versus-affine improvement claim.

Exact binomial intervals are an evaluated labeled-only comparator and the candidate's n<16 fallback. They anchor finite-sample coverage claims separately from the primary stabilized asymptotic interval.

The separate internal safety track bounds held-out residual and control means and combines component guarantees by a union bound. Source support justifies checking bound constants and assumptions, but no measured width or coverage advantage is attributed to this track.

Case 5 exhibits severe undercoverage and zero-width intervals for the implemented PPI++ baseline. The candidate uses Wilson-style stabilization, not an exact Wilson interval for fitted controls; foundational boundary-inference literature is needed to explain this distinction and the limits of empirical coverage checks.
